newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank lending falls 0.1 pct in March--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank lending falls 0.1 pct in March--BOJ.

text.p: Outstanding loans held by Japanese banks edged down 0.1 percent in March from a year earlier to 535.79 trillion yen, according to a monthly report by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) issued on Wednesday.
The figure is the daily average of the amount of outstanding loans by all types of Japanese banks over the month.
The daily average of loans outstanding at the nation's top 10 commercial banks, or "city" banks, stood at 247.30 trillion yen in March, up 0.3 percent from a year earlier.
Japan's three long-term credit banks saw their average lending fall 1.8 percent from a year earlier to 45.80 trillion yen.
At Japan's seven main trust banks, outstanding loans in March stood at 53.32 trillion yen, down 5.2 percent from a year earlier, the report said.
Lending by foreign banks in March stood at 6.82 trillion yen, up 20.8 percent from a year earlier, it said.
